summary: The Indonesia–Timor Leste Commission on Truth and Friendship was a truth commission jointly established by Indonesia and East Timor in August 2005 to investigate violence around the 1999 East Timor independence referendum and seek the "conclusive truth" about those events. After private hearings and document reviews, it delivered its final report on July 15, 2008 to the two nations' presidents. The report was fully endorsed by Indonesian President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono and marked the first government acknowledgement by Indonesia of human rights violations committed by state institutions in Timor. The commission is notable as the first modern bilateral truth commission.
one_line: A 2005–2008 bilateral truth commission set up by Indonesia and East Timor to investigate violence around the 1999 independence referendum.
key_facts: The Indonesia–Timor Leste Commission on Truth and Friendship was established jointly by the governments of Indonesia and East Timor in August 2005.
The commission was created to investigate acts of violence that occurred around the independence referendum held in East Timor in 1999.
The commission sought to find the "conclusive truth" behind the events surrounding the 1999 referendum.
The commission conducted private hearings and document reviews before producing its findings.
The commission handed its final report to the presidents of both nations on July 15, 2008.
Indonesian President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono fully endorsed the commission's final report.
The report provided the first acknowledgement by the government of Indonesia of human rights violations committed by state institutions in Timor.
The commission is notable for being the first modern truth commission to be bilateral.
